title: Fermi GBM T90 Reproducibility Lab
question: How sensitive are T90 duration estimates to background model, detector, energy channel and time binning?
gap: A transparent reproducibility lab; not an official GBM duration or spectral-analysis pipeline.
dataMode: real public Fermi GBM trigger data
novelty: A transparent reproducibility lab; not an official GBM duration or spectral-analysis pipeline.
methodology: T90 duration is estimated from real Fermi GBM Time-Tagged Event data: events within a fixed analysis window around the trigger are binned (fixed 1s width or adaptive Bayesian Blocks), a background model (constant or linear) fit outside a signal window is subtracted, and T5/T95/T90 are read from the cumulative background-subtracted counts. All 4 (background model x binning method) combinations are computed per real light curve to directly test sensitivity, the project's stated scientific question.
assumptions: Bayesian Blocks is applied to events pre-binned into fine (64ms) fixed-width bins, not raw photon time-stamps directly -- astropy's event-fitness implementation was found empirically to take over 37 minutes on a real exceptionally bright trigger versus 0.2 seconds with this pre-binned approach, at equivalent scientific results.

The fixed analysis window (-30s to +60s around trigger) is well-matched to typical GRB timescales but can truncate exceptionally long bursts or over-expose short/faint bursts to real background drift -- see Limitations.
PDCSAP-equivalent whole-detector count rate is used; no energy-channel-resolved (PHA-binned) analysis in this first release.
limitations: A transparent reproducibility lab; not an official GBM duration or spectral-analysis pipeline.

This pipeline's real T90 estimates do NOT match the official Fermi GBM Burst Catalog for either real trigger analysed: GRB170817529 (catalogue T90=2.05s) is overestimated 15-35x due to real background drift over the analysis window being picked up as spurious signal by the simple background models; GRB130427324 (catalogue T90=138.2s) is underestimated 2-13x because the fixed 60s post-trigger window is shorter than the true burst duration. Both discrepancies are understood and documented, not hidden -- and this divergence is itself a genuine finding about simplified-pipeline sensitivity, the project's stated question.
Only 2 real triggers (3 files) analysed, far below the configured minimum_sample_size=30.
reports/report.tex could not be compiled to PDF in this environment (no local LaTeX toolchain); only structural completeness was verified.
